subject: math
cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume
intro: Use facts about complementary, supplementary, vertical, and adjacent angles to write and solve an equation for each unknown. Remember: complementary angles sum to $90^\circ$, supplementary angles (a linear pair) sum to $180^\circ$, vertical angles are equal, and angles around a point sum to $360^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One of them measures $35^\circ$. Find the measure of the other angle.
Two angles are supplementary. One of them measures $118^\circ$. Find the measure of the other angle.
Two lines intersect. One of the four angles measures $73^\circ$. What is the measure of the angle vertical to it?

steps: Vertical angles are formed by two intersecting lines and are always equal (congruent).
The angle vertical to a $73^\circ$ angle has the same measure.

items.prompt: Angles $\angle ABD$ and $\angle DBC$ together form a straight line, so they are a linear pair. If $\angle ABD = 104^\circ$, find $\angle DBC$.

steps: A linear pair forms a straight angle, so the two angles sum to $180^\circ$.

items.prompt: Ray $BD$ lies inside right angle $\angle ABC$, splitting it into $\angle ABD$ and $\angle DBC$. If $\angle ABD = 28^\circ$, find $\angle DBC$.

steps: The two adjacent angles compose a right angle, so they sum to $90^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two lines intersect. One angle measures $(3x - 5)^\circ$ and its vertical angle measures $70^\circ$. Solve for $x$.

steps: Vertical angles are equal, so set the expressions equal: $3x - 5 = 70$.

items.prompt: An angle of measure $(2x + 10)^\circ$ is complementary to a $40^\circ$ angle. Find $x$ and the measure of the angle $(2x + 10)^\circ$.

steps: Substitute back: $2x + 10 = 2(20) + 10 = 50$, so the angle measures $50^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two supplementary angles measure $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and $(3x)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of both angles.
Ray $BD$ lies inside right angle $\angle ABC$. If $\angle ABD = (2x)^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = (x + 15)^\circ$, find $x$ and the measure of each angle.

steps: The two adjacent angles compose a right angle, so they sum to $90^\circ$: $2x + (x + 15) = 90$.
Substitute back: $\angle ABD = 2x = 50^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = x + 15 = 40^\circ$ (check: $50 + 40 = 90$).

items.prompt: Three angles meet at a point and together make a full turn: $(x)^\circ$, $(2x)^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. Find $x$.

steps: Angles around a point sum to $360^\circ$: $x + 2x + 150 = 360$.

items.prompt: Two lines intersect. One of the four angles measures $(4x + 8)^\circ$, and the adjacent angle on the line (its supplement) measures $(6x - 28)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of the larger of the two angles.

steps: The two adjacent angles form a linear pair, so they sum to $180^\circ$: $(4x + 8) + (6x - 28) = 180$.

items.prompt: Two intersecting lines form vertical angles. One angle measures $(5x + 3)^\circ$ and its vertical angle measures $(7x - 21)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of each of these vertical angles.

steps: Vertical angles are equal, so set the expressions equal: $5x + 3 = 7x - 21$.
Each of these vertical angles measures $63^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two lines intersect. One angle measures $(3x + 12)^\circ$. The angle adjacent to it on the line (its linear pair) measures $(x + 8)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of the angle that is vertical to the $(3x + 12)^\circ$ angle.

steps: The two adjacent angles form a linear pair summing to $180^\circ$: $(3x + 12) + (x + 8) = 180$.
Vertical angles are equal, so the angle vertical to the $132^\circ$ angle also measures $132^\circ$.

items.prompt: Four angles meet at a point and together make a full turn: $(2x)^\circ$, $(x + 10)^\circ$, $(3x)^\circ$, and $80^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of the largest of the three unknown angles.

steps: Angles around a point sum to $360^\circ$: $2x + (x + 10) + 3x + 80 = 360$.
The largest of the three unknown angles is $3x = 135^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two lines intersect at point $P$, and a third ray from $P$ splits one of the straight angles. Going around the straight line on one side, three adjacent angles measure $(x + 5)^\circ$, $(2x)^\circ$, and $(x - 1)^\circ$, and together they form a straight line. Find $x$ and the measure of the largest of these three angles.

steps: The three adjacent angles together form a straight angle, so they sum to $180^\circ$: $(x + 5) + 2x + (x - 1) = 180$.
The largest of these three angles measures $88^\circ$.
